name: Act of May 27, 1878 (Indian appropriations): removal of Chief Joseph's band of Nez Perce from Fort Leavenworth to the Indian Territory
aka: Indian Department appropriations act for fiscal year 1879, Nez Perces of Joseph's band item
nations: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation (descendants of Chief Joseph's band)
promises: This was an appropriation, not a treaty. Congress gave $20,000 for removing the Nez Perce of Joseph's band, then held as prisoners of war at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, to a suitable location in the Indian Territory, and for their settlement, clothing, subsistence and teaching.

Royce records that the band selected Townships 25 and 26 North, Ranges 1 and 2 West, in the Indian Territory, 90,710.89 acres, deeded by the Cherokee to the United States in trust for them (area 606).
landTaken: Royce area 606: the 90,710.89-acre reserve in the Indian Territory. Royce records that the band, determining to return to Idaho, deeded its claim to it to the United States on May 22, 1885.
compensation: None found for the 1885 deed of the Indian Territory reserve.
today: In Docket 179 the Colville Tribes, for Joseph's band, claimed the band's share of Nez Perce trust funds and allotments it never received; the Nez Perce Tribe of Idaho joined as intervenor, and the general accounting claim to June 30, 1951 was settled by compromise for a net judgment of $1,119,071.78 in favor of both in 1970, with no finding of liability. The Colville Tribes record that Chief Moses invited Joseph's band to the Colville Reservation in 1885 and that the government moved members of the band there in 1885 and later years. In Joseph's Band of the Nez Perce Tribe v. United States, 95 Ct. Cl. 11 (1941), the Court of Claims dismissed the band's claim to the Wallowa country, holding it bound by the 1863 treaty; that ruling concerns Wallowa, not this Act.

nationVoice.nation: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation
nationVoice.summary: The Colville Tribes' history records that in 1885 Chief Moses invited Chief Joseph and his band to stay on the Colville Reservation, and that the government moved members of the Joseph Band there from 1885.

openQuestions: treaties.json gives Oklahoma and only the Nez Perce Tribe of Idaho; most of Joseph's own band went to the Colville Reservation in 1885, so the Colville Tribes are added here. treaties.json was not edited.

Royce's remark (p. 893) says a reserve was bought for the band from the Cherokee out of the land west of 96 degrees and that the Cherokee deed is dated June 14, 1883. Removal 'west of the Kaws' and payment under the Act of March 3, 1881 belong to the Ponca entry printed beside it on the same page, not to this Act (audit 2026-11-08).
Whether anything was paid for the 90,710.89 acres the band deeded back on May 22, 1885, and what became of that land, was not traced.

No court or Commission finding about this Act or the Indian Territory reserve was located. The broken promise most often told, that the band would be returned to Idaho after its surrender in 1877, belongs to the 1877 surrender and was not researched here.
The Nez Perce Tribe's own account of the years in the Indian Territory was not located in this pass.

Audit 2026-11-08: 20 Stat. 74 (govinfo) and Royce pp. 892-893 reopened: the $20,000 item and the 90,710.89 acres confirmed. An earlier open question mixed in the Ponca remark from the same page (west of the Kaws, Act of March 3, 1881); corrected. Docket 179 settlement findings (OSU 2651) reread: the judgment ran to the Colville Tribes for Joseph's band and to the Nez Perce Tribe of Idaho as intervenor; today corrected.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Nez" (opened 95 Ct. Cl. 1, 95 Ct. Cl. 11, 176 Ct. Cl. 815) and ICC full text "Joseph band Indian Territory 1878", "Nez Perce Cherokee Outlet 1885", "Joseph Leavenworth Quapaw". Joseph's Band v. United States, 95 Ct. Cl. 11 (1941), dismissed the band's claim to the Wallowa country (it held the band bound by the 1863 treaty); that ruling against the band concerns Wallowa, not this Act. The Cherokee Outlet decision (Docket 173, OSU 60) lists the 90,710.89 acre reserve under this Act as Cherokee land; no finding for the Nez Perce. Nothing new.
